title: Zutty's temperament
summary: Roy talks about Zutty's moods and habit of dropping the volume.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What was the problem with Zutty? Was he temperamental?

I really don't know. I mean, he had problems with Louis, too, you know. I just really could never figure him out, you know. He always thought somebody was plotting against him or something. Like he would tell me, he said 'You ought to watch the trumpet ...(?)..., because they got black hearts' -- they're evil, you know.
And he always would pick on piano players, too. Man, he used to get Dick Wellstood.
I know that there would be sometimes different ideas about time and so on, I guess.
Yeah, but the piano player would be all right, you know what I mean... I don't think he messed with Cliff Jackson, though.
No, I liked Zutty a lot, but of course, I didn't have to work with him or anything.
I liked him, too. But I'd rather like him than to play with him, you know.

Well, see, I'll tell you one thing he had a habit of doing that I didn't like, you know. He would be swingin' like a dog, man. He'd build it up to where it's really going, and then he'd get to the middle, and he'd drop way down real soft, you know. And it would just cut your whole concentration and thinking, you know.
